agent_response:
PI-SLEEP-OK-0014

Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, identical subproblems. Each recursive call works on a reduced portion of the original problem until it reaches a base case—a condition where the answer is known without further recursion—which prevents infinite looping and allows the calls to unwind, combining their results back up the chain. It's essentially solving something by solving smaller versions of itself until you hit the trivial case, then building the solution back up.
